utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-96-23/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Zelenovic, before we continue, do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't see your answer yet on the transcript, but I think you said yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff. I appear here, accompanied by the case manager, Verica Balikic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Zoran Jovanovic. I'm representing Mr. Zelenovic, the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. We are here to hear a joint motion, a joint motion for consideration of a plea agreement between Dragan Zelenovic and the Office of the Prosecutor, pursuant to Rule 62 ter, which was filed on the 14th of December, confidentially. But this is a public hearing, and since plea agreements should be made public, we hear this motion in a public hearing. At least I did not see any request for keeping the plea agreement confidential, or is there any wish on behalf of the parties to keep parts - I wouldn't say the whole of the plea agreement - confidential?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. And as you can see from the filing that we would request in this hearing today that the Trial Chamber orders that the documentation attached to the motion be released as public documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jovanovic, therefore, we'll have a look at the plea agreement, what actually was agreed upon. The accused, Mr. Zelenovic, agreed, committed himself to enter a guilty plea on some of the charges. They are set out in paragraph 2. It would be a guilty plea to a total of seven counts, and they are specified in -- under 1 and 2 of paragraph 2 of the plea agreement. The Prosecution commits itself to dropping the remainder of the counts in the indictment. We will come to that in more detail at a later stage. Then there seems to be no agreement on what sentence should be proposed to the Trial Chamber. The Prosecution will recommend 10 to 15 years, and the Defence will recommend the Trial Chamber that it impose a term of imprisonment within the range of 7 to 10 years. So there's no full agreement, but the parties do understand from each other what to expect from the other party under this plea agreement. But there's no joint proposal for sentence. Then attached to the plea agreement is a factual basis on which the parties agree. We'll come to that in more detail in a moment as well. And then we have the, if I could call that, the -- we have a close cooperation by Mr. Zelenovic, and Mr. Zelenovic expresses in this plea agreement that he understands certain matters, one of them being that the Chamber is not bound by any agreement on sentencing, not even on the ranges expressed by the Prosecution, but that the Trial Chamber can impose a sentence of maximum -- a life sentence. Then there's another commitment of Mr. Zelenovic, saying that regardless of the sentence imposed, he will not move to withdraw his guilty plea or appeal his conviction pursuant to this guilty plea. Although it does not expressly say so, the Chamber understands this as Mr. Zelenovic would still be free to appeal against sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then in paragraph 15, there is an issue of the Chamber taking into consideration any prison sentence imposed to the extent already in force abroad. Is there any reason to believe for the parties that for the same acts, if ever a judgement was rendered in another country?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's no indication that this happened elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, then, the Chamber has some difficulty in understanding the relevance of putting this if there is no judgement, then -- because we might even be barred by a foreign judgement to exercise our jurisdiction. That takes quite a lot of things before we even could enter -- we could even come to a conviction, because that requires all kinds of additional matters, such as that it should not be a serious judgement, because otherwise we are barred by the nebis in idem. But I do understand that there is no practical reason to assume that there is any judgement anywhere for the same acts. Mr. Zelenovic in this plea agreement waives some of his rights, the right to plead not guilty. That goes almost without saying that if you plead guilty, you waive the right of pleading not guilty, the right to prepare and put forward a defence at a public trial, the right to be tried without undue delay, although it might even go quicker this way; the right to be tried in his presence. There will be no trial, just sentencing proceedings. The right to examine witnesses or have examined witnesses. The right not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt. Yes, of course, he waives the right to confess guilt because he pleads guilty. The right to testify, to remain silent, and the right to appeal a finding of guilty or to appeal any pre-trial rulings. This is, in short, the summary content of the plea agreement. Before we continue, I'd like to see whether the plea agreement is clear, whether it's -- whether there are any remaining questions in relation to the plea agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Moloto may have a few questions to the parties in respect of the content of the plea agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. With regard to paragraph 5 of the factual statement, there is a reference to -- under number 10, after referring to the 52 per cent, what I do want to understand is, is the number 10 the number of people or is that 10 per cent?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's actually 10 Muslims, as persons, that remained in Foca. Not 10 per cent but 10 persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ten persons, okay. Thank you very much. It is not absolutely clear to me, and it may very well be so that this paragraph refers to torture, but in paragraph 9, what crime is the accused alleged to have committed in that paragraph? Is that rape or torture? It may very well be that it's intended to be rape.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it should be rape and torture. It's actually cumulative charging.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there perhaps -- could I ask for a clarification. In the factual -- statement of facts, we, again, find rape, rape, rape, and never torture. Is it to be understood that the facts described in the factual statement on which the parties agree, although rape is mentioned again and again, that it would cover the torture charges of the indictment as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As you can see when you look into the particular charges, they relate, actually, to the conduct that is described in the paragraphs before the charges. And we always charged torture when the rape was actually related to, for instance, is in this case here interrogation. It was a punishment for not telling the truth. That's basically the torture motive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In that respect, can we then -- because there are more incidents of rape than the counts of rape themselves, or even the counts of rape and torture put together. My question then would be how do we compute a count for purposes of this agreement?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, you can actually see it from the indictment. When you, for instance, starting with the events in Buk Bijela, if you look at the charges as they relate to Mr. Zelenovic, you can see that for all the conduct that is related to Buk Bijela, Mr. Zelenovic is actually charged cumulatively for torture and rape. So there is in all these -- in all these incidents, there is always torture and always rape charged. That same -- the same applies to the charges in relation to the Foca High School. You can also -- when you look at the -- at torture charges, count 13, you see also that it relates to all the incidents that were described in the paragraphs above. The same applies to Partizan Sports Hall. If you look at -- let me just see. If you look at Count 41, you have, again, the torture charge. And in the line above, you can see that they apply to all the acts that are described in the paragraphs above. And finally, when it comes to the event in the fish restaurant, here, you have actually the only situation where only rape is charged. If you look at count 49, that's on the last page of the indictment, here you have the event in the fish restaurant and -- above the fish restaurant, actually, and here you see only a rape charge, because this event is not related to any interrogation situation or any other situation that includes torture purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. If we look again at paragraph 13 of the factual basis, there seems to be a reference here to three occasions when FWS-75 and FWS-87 were taken to an apartment building called Brena. And then the paragraph goes on to talk about the first occasion when the accused and others are alleged to have raped FWS-75 in various ways, and then the accused is also mentioned in respect of FWS-87. I'm not quite sure now where is the third occasion where this happened within this paragraph, or is the third occasion been -- there in the next paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it's actually -- let me just see. In paragraph 13, we have actually three occasions where these two victims were raped in the apartment building Brena block --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- and the next paragraph, 14, deals with two further occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But if you read paragraph 13, it says that between about the 18th of July and about the 13th of July, 1992, on three occasions, these two people were taken from Foca High School to an apartment building called Brena in the centre of Foca. The building was near the Zelengora hotel and military headquarters of the Bosnian Serb forces. Then in the same paragraph you then say, the first time the women went to an apartment owned by Dragan Zelenovic. I'm anticipating that within that paragraph you must tell me about the second and the third time, because -- now, the second and third time could not be in the next paragraph if you're dealing with the three occasions in paragraph 13. This is the lack of clarity that I find. I'm not quite sure, because there's no further reference to the second and third time in this paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you are right. It's actually -- I've now looked at the indictment again. It's actually -- 6.8 is one rape and 6.9 are the two other rapes. They are already indicated in the first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In the first one?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. The first one refers to three occasions and describes the first one, and the next paragraph refers to the other two occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But then from a structural point of view, is that proper? Is that helpful, to refer in one paragraph to three occasions and then deal with only one occasion and then move on to the next paragraph which doesn't refer to the three occasions and then deal with parts of the last paragraph in that paragraph? My difficulty is, I found it very difficult to marry the incidents in the agreement with the indictment. And when one says that the accused is pleading guilty to seven counts, three of which are torture and four of which are rape, I would like to be able to see in the agreement what actual counts in the indictment the accused is admitting to. This is my difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, the indictment is actually charging in each of the counts several incidents. The first group of incidents are actually the one related to Buk Bijela. That's just one count of rape and one count of torture. And then there comes the next -- the next occasion. That's the Foca High School. And you have only one torture charge and one rape charge, although you have several incidents. And that's the same with the Partizan Sports Hall and the same -- the last, the fish restaurant, is just one single rape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if you look at the structure of the indictment, it starts, when it comes to the explanation regarding the charges, it starts with an overall count. For instance, when you look at 6.6 -- sorry, I'm now in the wrong -- if you start again with Buk Bijela, the first paragraph describes the general events there and then followed by the separate rapes. And that's the same with the situation in the Partizan Sports Hall that Your Honour referred to or in the Foca High School; that first you have an overall description of what happened and how often things happen and then you have the description of the separate rapes and incidents. And there shouldn't be any problems because all incidents actually are combined in one charge of torture and one charge of rape. So if the accused, as he actually did say, I didn't do incident 6.5 or whatever, then you can easily actually see what the factual basis relates to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the factual basis, you always find -- after a description, you always find a reference to the appropriate paragraph in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I didn't think I'd found that, actually. Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's actually always at the end of the paragraph. It refers to the paragraph in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And so it may be complicated, Your Honour, and it may have been easier to perhaps change things more than we did, but I thought it's understandable with the reference to the incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question: Do I understand you to be saying the incidents under Buk Bijela constitute one charge, one count?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The incidents under Foca High School constitute another count.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then also Partizan and then also the fish restaurant. So it's four incidents --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's four locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Four locations, all of which are rape, the first three of which are torture, are torture and rape -- the first three are torture and rape, the last is rape.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Hence three counts of torture, four counts of rape.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's how you explain it, in short?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It would have been very helpful if, perhaps, after Buk Bijela it was written count 1, and then after Foca, count 2, whatever the number. But I now understand what you say. I'm not quite sure whether the explanation you gave is sufficient or whether it requires the document or an amended indictment or an amended statement of agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still have some problems with it. Could we perhaps do an exercise on one of the examples --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and then go back to the indictment. Foca High School. Judge Moloto has already asked for your clarification on the indictment, 6.8, where you say 6.8 describes one incident and that's, therefore, a mistake. It says that on three occasions, one of them is only covered by 6.8, and you say the other two are covered by 6.9, where it is between the 8th of July and about the 13th of July, 1992, on two occasions, you say the other two are remaining.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So where is 6.10 on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's another occasion, but you can distinguish it here because it's a different location where the rape occurs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Different location?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. If you see here, 6.10 happens in an abandoned house of a Muslim policeman in Gornje Polje. That's a distinguishing factor. It's a rape at the same point in time but at a different location and actually including a third victim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although it's still Foca High School --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so we have two levels of locations. One we find in the headings, but there are differences in location within the paragraphs as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And there's also -- in Foca High School, you actually have also in 6.6 the location where the women are actually raped in the high school itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's now clear to me. Now, we have -- so if there is an agreement that Mr. Zelenovic pleads guilty to count 13, which -- yes, in count 13, as we find it under 2(ii), two counts charge crime against humanity, torture, and 13 and 14, that's torture and rape, that covers, as is said, 6.8, 6.9, and 6.10, from what I read in 2, under -- on page 2 of the indictment. So 6.8, 6.9 and 6.10 in the indictment are covered by count 13, so a guilty plea --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What you need to read is actually -- when you look into the plea agreement, paragraph 2, you have to read the chapter (i) and (ii) in conjunction. You can see here we have listed the paragraphs, and Foca High School, that's 6.6, 6.8, 6.9 and 6.10, and I think you omitted 6.6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But since I started asking questions starting with 6.8, I limited it to that. But I fully agree that 6.6 is ... Now, I would like to focus on 6.8, 6.9, 6.10, because you explained that 6.8 is -- although it says three occasions, describes only the first incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then 6.9, we find the two remaining incidents that were referred to in 6.8.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now in 6.10, you say there is another incident on a slightly different location. That's the abandoned house. So if Mr. Zelenovic pleads guilty to count 13, does he plead guilty to 6.6, 6.8, 6.9 and 6.10, all these incidents?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if I look at the agreement of facts, I see no reference to the victim ZG who is mentioned in 6.10. How do I have to understand that? I mean Mr. Zelenovic took ZG to that abandoned house where she was raped by an unidentified soldier. Is that torture, bringing her there and allowing that she was raped by this unidentified soldier? Is this aiding and abetting to this rape and to torture by bringing her there? ZG is not mentioned in any way in the agreement on facts. Nevertheless, it is covered by 6.10 and therefore would fall within the scope of a guilty plea on count 13, although nothing is said about it in the agreement on facts, the factual statement. Could you explain that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as I remember, the reason for not putting ZG into number 15 was that Mr. Zelenovic did not remember ZG and we wanted to base the guilty plea on what he actually, himself, remembers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So his guilty plea on 13, counts 13 and 14, would not cover, as is said in the plea agreement, the whole of 6.10, but would cover only part of 6.10 and would, as a matter of fact, in respect of witness -- of victim ZG, would be a not guilty plea, a plea of not guilty, because, as you said, he doesn't remember he wants to admit guilt on victim ZG.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honour, is that he actually admits to have raped -- has actually taken part in the incident 6.10 and admits to it, but that he only does not recall a third person being present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So I think he pleads guilty to 6.10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To everything, also to ZG? Even if he doesn't remember, he nevertheless pleads guilty on victim ZG?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think so. I think he should be asked about this. It was my understanding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's ask Mr. Jovanovic on how he understands this. Mr. Jovanovic, as a matter of fact, I'd like to stress that whenever Madam Uertz-Retzlaff says anything about explaining what the plea agreement says, that of course if you disagree, I would expect you to jump up immediately and to inform us that that is not your understanding of the plea agreement. But specifically now your view is asked on counts 13 and 14 in relation to paragraph 6.10 of the indictment mentioning victim ZG, where we do not find anything about -- in the statement of facts about victim ZG.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I was sure I would have a chance to say what I have to say about this. The plea agreement is quite clear. It refers to only two victims, FWS-75 and FWS-87. In the statement of facts, the Prosecution agreed to orally amend the indictment rather than amending the indictment in writing. Our understanding was that Mr. Dragan Zelenovic would plead guilty to events concerning victims FWS-75 and FWS-87, not any other victim mentioned in the indictment. Therefore, the Defence expects the Prosecution to amend the description of events mentioned in paragraph 6.10 of the indictment as it refers to victim ZG.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, where do I exactly find this definition of pleading guilty in respect of victims FWS-75 and 87? Because what I find, as a matter of fact, in 2(i) and 2(ii) is not a reference to victims but a reference to paragraphs in the indictment, one of them clearly including victim ZG, and that's in 6.10. So where do I read in the agreement that it's based on the identity of the victims, as you just mentioned them, rather than paragraphs of the indictment and counts of the indictment? Could you point to me, where do I find this? Is there any reference at all to the identity of the victims, not in the statement of facts but in the plea agreement? Perhaps Madam Uertz-Retzlaff could assist you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, in the plea agreement, references are actually made to the incident Mr. Zelenovic accepted, and wherever he actually accepted that other victims were involved, it is expressed in the factual basis. But in relation to ZG, as she's not mentioned here, he did not agree that she was present, or rather didn't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, you now expect this Chamber to accept a guilty plea on counts and paragraphs of the indictment clearly described - and I'm focusing now on 6.10 - where we find his involvement in victim ZG being raped, he would then plead guilty to count 13, he would plead guilty specifically in respect of the incident described in 6.10, and now we have to deduce from the statement of facts that this, of course, does not include one of the victims described in 6.10? Is that what you expect this Chamber to do? And for you the same, Mr. Jovanovic. How are we going to receive such a plea? We say Mr. Zelenovic, do you plead guilty to, or not guilty to count 13, covering paragraphs so and so and so. He says yes. And then somewhere in the back of our mind, it should be that this does not include one of the victims specifically mentioned in 6.10.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually we thought that we could clarify this when he pleads to the particular counts, if he would -- he would, for instance, say, when it comes to the count 13, he would say, including the incidents, numbering them, and say in relation to 6.10, this does not include the victim ZG. This is actually what we had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Usually, as you know, if the Chamber is inviting an accused to enter a plea, we usually ask him whether he pleads guilty or not guilty and not to give a full statement of what is included and what is not included, et cetera. That at least for me would be a totally new procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What I actually could propose, Your Honour, is we could redact the indictment, and actually redacting everything not pleaded to. That means we could redact the paragraphs that are now -- that are not pleaded to, the paragraphs -- the incidents, basically, and also redact, if it is as in 6.10, redact in 6.10 the victim ZG. And we could actually redact everything that he's not pleading to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would it not be helpful, madam, if you perhaps formulated an amended indictment, including only the incidents admitted to? Then when we say, "Mr. Zelenovic, do you plead guilty to count 6 as amended," then he pleads to guilty to count 6 as amended, and specifying only the incidents he admits to. Would it -- that would cut across the whole problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: If you prefer this. I thought the redactions would actually have the same purpose. But if you prefer to have an amended indictment, of course we can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The amended indictment is that it would be short and sweet and concise, to the point, and it would only deal with the issues that he admits to and you don't have to look at what has been redacted and what has not been redacted. You can say this document, as it stands, encompasses the entire incidents that the accused admits, and we put that to him and he agrees to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll see how we proceed. We might have some other questions as well. You drew my attention, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, to 6.6 earlier. In 6.6, for example, we find victim FWS-50. That is 6.6 to which the accused committed to plead guilty as well under count 13 and 14. But do I now have to understand that FWS-50 is not included in the guilty plea, just as ZG would not be included in the guilty plea?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the incident involving, actually, five women is included in the guilty plea but not the identity of the women. So the accused actually says, "I was involved in taking out five victims --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- but not specifying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So not necessarily FWS-50. So if there would be a guilty plea on counts 13 and 14 in relation to 6.6, that would be a guilty plea on this incident but not including the identity at least of these --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Other three, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- other --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, other two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It leaves a lot of guessing, which the Chamber is not very much in favour of if we're talking about guilty pleas. Okay. At least we have to find a solution for this. Let's see whether there are any other questions. Let me just have a look. One second. You said there were five women in 6.6 --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Four. I made a mistake, Your Honour. Four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. So it's not the other three but the other two. Yes. Now I understand. This has been clarified by now, because I couldn't find the five. Now let's see whether all the -- may I ask your attention to paragraph 9 of the factual statement. We see that Mr. Zelenovic is not charged with raping, himself, victim FWS-75. How do we have to understand his participation, apart from I do understand it's torture. But he didn't rape her. Is it co-perpetratorship? Is it aiding and abetting? How do we have to understand this?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to point 9, it's aiding and abetting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is aiding and abetting, okay. So, as a matter of fact, in relation to -- let me just find the ... We find that in the indictment exactly in paragraph -- paragraph 9 would be 5.4 in the indictment; is that correct? Where, now, is the aiding and abetting --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's 5.4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where do we find that a guilty plea in relation to 5.4 would be pleading guilty to aiding and abetting to this incident? Where do I find that? It's a form of responsibility, which is not ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's not in there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not in there. Okay. Let's see whether there are any other matters. We have to turn to, I think, paragraph 19 of the factual statement. Yes. In paragraph 19 of the factual statement, it says, "After July --" "During July 1992, Dragan Zelenovic took FWS-87 from Partizan and gang-raped her along with three other co-perpetrators." Is that one incident? Because 19 starts with a pattern of sexual assaults commenced. "Armed soldiers, Muslim groups of three to five, entered Partizan usually in the evenings and removed --" Is Mr. Zelenovic -- he is charged with one rape or with more rapes?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. One rape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just one rape. Of course that's enough. Then the issue of rape and torture you have clarified. Is it always clear for all of these incidents - because to me it's not, although the general description is that women were taken and were interrogated - but for each of the incidents, the link with the interrogations is not always explicit. Do I have to understand this: That you link the rape and the whole of the context with interrogations or -- because not always we see a clear link between interrogations, denying to answer and then a rape. Is it a general link that you consider to be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not only -- the torture charge is not only related to interrogation, it's also related, as it says in the -- I think it should say -- actually, in the general allegations, it should be specified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General allegations in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not. I thought it was but it's not. You can -- in relation to the torture counts, there's not only the purpose of interrogation but also the torture purpose of discrimination. It says, actually, in the plea agreement, under paragraph 5, it refers to the torture -- the torture purposes that are actually mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it refers to punishment, intimidation, coercion of a third person, or discrimination as ground for the purpose -- the torture charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's not particularly specified in the indictment which one applies, but it's here mentioned in the -- in the plea agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you said that in the count in the indictment where only rape is charged - that was, I think, 41 --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, it's the last incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that not discriminatory, then, or -- you explained to us why it was -- no, it's not 41, it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's 49, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 49, yes. Was there no discrimination there? You explained to us why it was just rape, and you said it was because there was no interrogation. I now understand that it's not only interrogation but discrimination which raises immediately the question whether the rape, under count 49, was not of a discriminatory nature.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we decided it to charge it this way, and it's a long time ago. I must admit I do not recall it any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you gave us an explanation a minute ago why it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, but I do not recall the reason why in this particular incident we did only charge rape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When it would come to your mind, then we'd like to further hear from you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I seem to recall, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- when you look at the indictment, what we have here, the other two locations are actually camp locations where the women were actually abused and taken away in the front of others, terrifying others, showing openly to the audience what is happening or going to happen to the victims. And here with the last rape, it's sort of a different scenario. I seem to recall that that was the reason why we said this was more the regular rape scenario, while in the other incidents, with the camp situation and all the other victims that were detained watching what's going on, that has quite a different impact on the group of the victims as such, as the Muslim -- as the Muslims as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It now seems that the public character, more or less, becomes the criteria rather than --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I seem to recall that we made a distinction between the two scenarios.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear to me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I understand that the other one was done in private?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. The women were actually taken away from Karaman's House, relocated to Foca, and in the course of this relocation, they were raped as one incident in the fish -- above the fish restaurant, and it was not so obvious to other groups of victims. At that time there was no -- the groups of victims that were actually taken from the villages were no more together, and it was -- it had, in the other locations, the effect that the women were taken out and raped. It was actually also a huge impact on the other victims that were not raped at that time, but it had a severe impact on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What then constitutes torture from the point of view of the Prosecution? Is it the public nature of the incident --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, the purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, fair enough. The purpose could be, we're going to do it publicly so as a intimidate and terrorise the audience as well as the victims. But I'm asking you, what is the purpose, from the point of view of the Prosecution, that what constitutes torture? Is it the public nature of the incident? Is it the discriminatory nature of the incident? Or is it what you mentioned in the beginning which was that a -- I can't remember now, the very first reason why you distinguished between the three occasions and the last occasion. You gave a reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have listed in the plea agreement the situations of torture, the torture purposes that applied in this case, and it is actually -- the first one is obtaining information or confession. That is clearly related to Buk Bijela. And the second one is actually punishing and intimidating or coercion of victim or third person; that is clearly related to the other camp conditions. And finally there is also discrimination that also applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So do I understand you well that you say that by the incident near to the fish restaurant, there was not like in other situations intimidation of third persons --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- who were observing the victims to be taken away for purposes of being raped, where to that extent there were no third persons present there?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that was the distinction, I think, that we made at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there's still discrimination, or is it not?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So for that reason, torture could have been there under --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, but we have chosen not to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That at least answers some of the questions. Now, you've just told us that victim ZG was not included in the agreement because Mr. Zelenovic did not remember witness ZG. At the same time we see that the victims, for example, FWS-50, which he doesn't remember, is still included as one out of four women. Was the position -- perhaps I'd better ask Mr. Jovanovic. Is the position that the witness ZG and the other two witnesses that are, I would say, more or less, excluded from the guilty plea - these are -- let me just have a look. These are witnesses -- well, the two other witnesses - let me just find them - that Mr. Zelenovic -- it is witness FWS-95 and FWS-50. Is it that Mr. Zelenovic does not remember their identity or does he not remember that they were victimised -- no, it is 48, 50, and 95. What's the position of the Defence to enter a plea of not guilty in relation to these victims?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I have already mentioned, the view of the Defence and Mr. Zelenovic himself is that he accepts the events alleged in relation to FWS-75 and 87. So I don't think that it is correct to say that he does not remember their identity. He simply does not plead guilty in relation to the events as described in the indictment in which the victims were 48, FWS-48 and 95 and ZG. So that's our agreement with the Prosecution. And as I have already said, we have the agreement that the Prosecution was going to amend the indictment orally here today at this hearing. That's what we expected. So let me repeat: Mr. Zelenovic does not plead guilty about the events in which other victims were involved, except FWS-75 and 87.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, perhaps I should ask Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, it seems that for unknown reasons, apart from the four persons I just mentioned, for unknown reasons, Mr. Zelenovic does not plead guilty, whether he doesn't remember their identity or whether for any other reason, on charges you've brought against him and where the Confirming Judge has established that there's a prima facie case for that. What's your view on what this means for the other victims, the victims to which Mr. Zelenovic does not plead guilty and where you stated in the beginning of the proceedings that you had a prima facie case? And have you discussed with Mr. Jovanovic that in order to amend the indictment, you need the approval of the Chamber? I mean, let me put it quite bluntly: To what extent is the Prosecution involved in an exercise in which half of the victims are just devictimised for unknown reasons?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was a long discussion between the Prosecution and the Defence, and I actually have a memo on what the discussion was. And the position of Mr. Zelenovic always was, "I admit to certain incidents, but I have no recollection of being Foca 8, involved FWS-50, being FWS-95 involved." This is why the factual basis actually refers -- and ZG. I forgot to mention here. This is why the factual basis refers in these cases to either not mentioning a third women, like in the case of ZG, or in the other cases, referring to other women, two other women or referring to -- yeah, basically two other women. And that's -- that was the agreement, that when Mr. Zelenovic does not recall certain victims, but it was clear from the evidence in the Kunarac case that in a certain incident, four women were involved, then actually the four women are mentioned in the factual basis but only given the two identities that Mr. Zelenovic knows about. Because if all the victims basically say, "We were taken out in a group from the classroom in Foca High School and Mr. Zelenovic took us out, and we were four," then it can't be that in the factual basis and in the plea that it's only two now. But where -- where Mr. Zelenovic, on the other hand, says, "I do recall the incident as such with the four women, but I don't know two identities," then that's why we changed it. So that's why the incident in 6.6 involves four victims and the incidents above the fish restaurant involves four victims. We're not actually dropping those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless it seems that Mr. Jovanovic has a bit of a different understanding of the plea agreement. He says that the not guilty pleas are not based on not knowing the identity, because we are now faced with a not easy situation. There will be a guilty plea on count 49, from what I understand. Let me just verify that. A guilty plea on 49 with two witnesses mentioned by name and two witnesses of which we do not have the identity. Mr. Zelenovic pleads guilty also to the two other women. For Mr. Jovanovic, I understand that he says there's a guilty plea only on FWS-75 and 87, not on anyone else. And he also says that the pleas of not guilty on the other counts is not because he doesn't remember the identity. The Chamber is puzzled by where it takes it that the Confirming Judge considered to be a prima facie there, that just on the basis of Mr. Zelenovic saying, "I do not remember," to just take out these victims. And the other issue being that Mr. Jovanovic tells us that it's only 75 and 87, whereas you explained to us that count 49, under 9.1 in the indictment, covers two known and two unknown women, that Mr. Jovanovic seems to suggest that it's only 75 and 87. Could you, perhaps, clarify? Is there a misunderstanding, Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, if you look at paragraph 22 of the -- of the factual basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- it's clearly here stating, "on or about 30 October 1992, victim 75 and 87 and two other females were taken from Karaman's House."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- "and were raped in the apartment above the fish restaurant." And Mr. Zelenovic rapes 87.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I agree that it's in the factual statement, but Mr. Jovanovic tells us it's only 75 and 87. I hate to use only the numbers. Mr. Jovanovic, would I have to understand your earlier remark that it was only a guilty plea on victims FWS-75 and 87 to be extended also to unknown victims or unidentified victims specifically mentioned in the counts, in the incidents, and in the factual statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is precisely what it says in paragraph 2 of the factual basis. This is what Mr. Zelenovic accepted. He accepted that on that occasion women FWS-75 and 87 were taken out, plus two other women. So that is not contentious. But for him to say that he doesn't remember or doesn't know the identity, that allows for the possibility that these were the victims stated in the indictment. However, Mr. Zelenovic simply cannot accept the counts for torture and rape of 48, 95 and ZG, which was described in paragraph 60. His plea agreement covers his admission of events in relation to 75 and 87 and the events as described in paragraph 2 -- 22, namely, that two other women were present. However, the formulation cannot be such that those two other women were mentioned in the indictment but were not 75 and 87.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you say in 60, paragraph 60, he could not accept that. Is that because he says that such an incident did not take place, or does he say "it may have taken place but I don't remember," or "I do not remember whether these women were victims in such an incident"?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me make a correction. It says paragraph 60 in the transcript, whereas what I had in mind was the paragraph of the indictment 6.10, where it says that an unidentified soldier raped ZG; that is to say, that Mr. Zelenovic does not accept responsibility for this rape of victim ZG by an unidentified soldier. And this is why the Defence insisted that the victim ZG, as described in paragraph 6.10 of the indictment, not be included in the statement of facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, and that's the basic question, if he says "I can't plead guilty," of course he's not under any duty -- he's entirely free to plead guilty or not guilty, but the Chamber will be confronted with a different matter, and that is if the supporting material for the indictment strongly supports that not only victims 75 and 87 were victims of these crimes but others as well, whether the Chamber is much inclined to say a guilty plea on one or two victims and that is good enough, in other words, let the rest go. Therefore, more or less, I'm inquiring into what is the basis of your agreement on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the basis of the -- when discussing the different incidents, the Prosecution looked, of course, what was the outcome of the Kunarac case and we also looked at the statements that were given by the victims involved. And in relation to, for instance, the fish restaurant incident or the first incident in the Foca High School, the witnesses are very precise. They said, "Four of us were taken and we were raped by the perpetrators, including Mr. Zelenovic." In relation to the incident involving ZG, only, as far as I remember it now correctly, only one of the victims - I think it's 75 - actually said, "We were three." And I seem -- so many details, but I seem to recall that the other one did not mention ZG. But I would have to check that now. And that was always then the result, as it is not 100 per cent clear whether it was ZG involved there. And that's actually the incident here that is -- that we are most concerned with. That's why we then dropped ZG.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I do understand that whenever you accepted an agreement on a non-guilty plea, that you had in the back of your mind that you might face some problems in producing sufficient evidence; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's the point. And also -- I have to also stress the point that in the Kunarac case, Mr. Zelenovic, of course, was not an issue, so the witnesses were not really asked much during that trial about Mr. Zelenovic. So a lot of details that now relate to Mr. Zelenovic's involvement were not fully explored in the case that has already been run here. So we actually did make some concessions from the side of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But always in view of potential, let's say, risks in the procedure that you might not be in a position to produce sufficient evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. We looked at the evidence that we had, and where we also had some differences in the statements of the victims, we actually felt it was better to actually make a decision in favour of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I add one more point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- and that relates actually to the victim 48 which we also do not find in the charges here. The judgement, the Kunarac judgement, was also not based on her evidence, because this victim was raped so often that she could not identify any more the particular incident and the particular perpetrators. Therefore, also in the Kunarac case, the evidence of this victim also, it was believed, was not actually used for the conviction, because that was really a problem with that victim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I do understand. We'll have a break now. The Chamber -- one of the things the Chamber will do during the break is to consider whether we could proceed on the basis of the -- of the plea agreement as we find it here, with all the confusion, where it's not clearly set out what a guilty plea on count so and so in relation to incident so and so would actually mean, whether it would cover all the victims or whether it would cover only one of the victims. We'll consider whether we can proceed on the basis of the existing plea agreement, and then, of course, we'd have to specify in quite some detail, when inviting the accused to enter a plea, or whether we would require the parties to be more clear in their agreement so that we avoid whatever confusion when asking from the accused to enter his pleas. We'll adjourn for half an hour. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let us see whether there are any questions remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've got one last question in relation to the factual statements -- factual statement. In paragraph 8, it reads at the end, "On or about the 3rd of July, 1992, during and after the interrogation, Dragan Zelenovic and the other co-perpetrators gang-raped several of the women they suspected of lying, in particular ..." How does the Chamber understand "in particular"? Is that, apart from the incidents mentioned, I take it, in 9 and 10, there may have been more which are not specified, or is it limited to the incident mentioned in 9 and 10?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is limited to the two incidents mentioned here, but of course in Buk Bijela, more perpetrators were involved in other incidents but they are not charged in relation to Mr. Zelenovic. As you see, the other indictment includes a lot of -- a lot more incidents than actually are redacted, and they relate to other perpetrators. That's why it says here "in particular." That's why the words are used. But, of course, the accused Zelenovic is only -- it's only -- is only charged in relation to these two incidents, and he also only admits these two incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it, Mr. Jovanovic, that you agree with this, which is, I would say, the favourable explanation to Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that is how the Defence understands the statement of facts as it relates to paragraphs 9 and 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. The Chamber has considered how to proceed. The Chamber is not satisfied with the plea agreement as a written basis for receiving pleas from this accused. The Chamber would very much like the parties to produce this same afternoon, as an annex to your plea agreement, a copy of the indictment in which you strike out exactly all parts to which Mr. Zelenovic does plead not guilty. For example, this would mean that, on the basis of what we heard, that in 6.10, victim ZG would be removed, and the rape of witness ZG, because Mr. Zelenovic is charged with involvement in that and I do understand that he pleads not guilty to that. If you would produce such a document this afternoon, we would have clear guidance to continue tomorrow and to invite Mr. Zelenovic to enter pleas on the counts with clear specification of which incidents are covered by the counts and whether the whole of the incidents or only part of the incidents are covered by the plea to be entered. We'll then proceed to asking Mr. Zelenovic to plea on those counts and those incidents as specified in this document. And from the plea agreement, I understand that then the Prosecution will ask for approval of withdrawing the remaining counts or portions of counts. The Chamber will then deal with that, and then we could conclude tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me ask a clarification. What -- it's clear for ZG, to actually simply strike her, but in -- and also we have discussed the fish restaurant incident which isn't a problem because it doesn't specify the two other women involved. But in relation to the incident 6.6 --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- we have actually the witnesses mentioned, 50 and 95, and the position of the accused here is that, "Yes, I did rape four victims, but I'm not able to say it's 50 and 95." That would mean 17 That's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether it's adding or not. What could be said is selected, and then give an X or a Y, if that is what is on your mind. But I do understand that there is an agreement on a guilty plea on the other two women, although unidentified.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that, Mr. Jovanovic, how you understand the plea agreement as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, specifically in reference to paragraph 6.6, the witnesses mentioned here, or rather the victims, are FWS-50, 75, 87 and 95, and Dragan Zelenovic is charged with raping FWS-75 and that is the plea he entered. Neither in the indictment nor in the plea agreement is it stated that Dragan Zelenovic raped four women. Therefore, in the factual statement, it is stated that he was among a group of soldiers which separated off four women, including these two, and that he raped 75, not as my learned friend said, that he raped four women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, I do understand that his involvement, although he did not rape the other women himself, is considered by the Prosecution to be aiding and abetting to the rape committed by others, although -- is that ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that actually was my next question that I wanted to raise. In relation to this incident, we actually see the four perpetrators doing the rapes as co-perpetrators. It's not aiding and abetting but it's co-perpetration. Only in relation to the Buk Bijela incident, that's -- the Buk Bijela incident -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now see that there seems to be a basic disagreement on what Mr. Zelenovic is charged with under 6.6. You say it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. He's actually -- he is in a group of four people, and he's actually the man in charge. He's the man who, in this incident, is actually dividing the victims among the perpetrators. So that's co-perpetration. In contrast to that, so that also Mr. Jovanovic understands it now more fully, in relation to the incident with the victim 75 being raped at Buk Bijela, the man Gojko Jankovic is in charge and Mr. Zelenovic is basically aiding and abetting here in this incident 5.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's the distinction to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff tells us that a guilty plea on 6.6 would include a guilty plea to co-perpetration of the rapes committed by others against victims that were not raped personally by Mr. Zelenovic. Is there agreement? And apart from whether he could identify the other victims by their pseudonyms, is that your understanding of the agreement on 6.6 as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I abide by the standpoint that Mr. Zelenovic can identify only witnesses 75 and 87. In paragraph 12 of the statement of facts, it is already stated that together with other co-perpetrators from the group, he separated off four women and girls -- he selected four women and girls from the classroom in which the detainees were kept. I understand Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff to say that he raped four women. However, it is the standpoint of the Defence -- I do apologise, then. It must be my mistake. It must be misinterpretation. But the factual statement actually does include co-perpetration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, co-perpetration --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But not identifying the other victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Co-perpetration of rape of four victims, two of them being identified as FWS-75 and 87, the other two, in the admission of guilt, not identified specifically as the persons mentioned in the indictment. Yes, that's clear. Then, as an annex -- we're just talking at this moment about an annex to the plea agreement and not yet an amendment of the indictment. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, I think then you could replace FWS-50 and FWS-95 by X and Y, which stands for victims not further identified by the accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That leaves, actually, one difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And that relates to the Buk Bijela rape of 75 where the position is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm talking now about paragraph 5.3 in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Where, actually, Mr. Zelenovic is party to the interrogation process that leads finally to the gang-rape of 75. And it's the position, the joint position, that this is only aiding and abetting to the gang-rape of 75. And that's not entirely clear from the indictment. Therefore, either a sentence is added to paragraph 4.6 in the indictment, where the mode of liability is mentioned. We could here add a sentence that, in relation to 5.3, aiding and abetting is charged. Or the other option is that in 5.9, that's the sentence immediately foregoing count 5 and count 6, one could also mention here, by the foregoing acts and omissions in relation to the victim 75, Dragan Zelenovic aided and abetted; 2, in relation to the victim FWS-87, Dragan Zelenovic committed. And I think that also would clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would be sufficient. So what the Chamber then expects is an attachment to the plea agreement which further specifies on what exactly the parties agreed by striking out anything on which it is not agreed; by striking out and putting in bold anything that further specifies, for example, unknown identity by X or Y, or by adding words "aiding and abetting." Please put that in bold clearly visible for the Chamber. And then we can proceed on the basis of this document to receive pleas tomorrow with the necessary level of detail which would avoid confusion as to what exactly the conviction will be about. Is there any other matter at this moment the parties would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. In principle, we agree that the other victims be identified as X and Y. I just want to make it clear that the standpoint of the Defence, which I have reiterated more than once, is that this will not refer to those victims who are mentioned in the indictment who are not 75 and 87; that in no way will it be stated that these are 50, 95, ZG and 48 whose testimony was not accepted by the Chamber in Kunarac et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I do understand that wherever in the indictment, as you will produce this afternoon, if a witness identified by a pseudonym where the accused does not admit that it was this witness that was a victim of that rape but admits that a woman was a victim of rape at that time, that then the identification through the pseudonym will be replaced by a general identification, by a letter X or Y. I am not very much inclined to enter into any further discussions on what should be in and what should not be in. That's a matter for the parties. And it only shows that it's good for the Chamber to ask for the position. So I leave it up to you. We'll see whether we receive this afternoon this clarification. If so, fine; if not, there's no basis to further hear any pleas on the basis of an agreement which seems to be incomplete. The parties should agree on the matter, not the Chamber. Anything else? Mr. Zelenovic, I would like to ask you, because you are not participating in this exchange of views, first of all, could you follow the discussions, and are you in agreement with all the further details and positions given by counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because tomorrow we'll have to establish, if we have received this new attachment to -- this new annex to the plea agreement, we'll have to establish whether you voluntarily and with full understanding entered into this agreement. Therefore, I want to verify at this moment whether you could follow it and whether you agree with everything that has been said. You'll be given an opportunity tomorrow to briefly consult with counsel to see what exactly then remains. Mr. Jovanovic, perhaps you could try to make a copy of the B/C/S version so that Mr. -- you don't have to produce a B/C/S version of this stricken-out indictment to the Chamber. We'll be happy with the English version. But if you do a similar exercise for Mr. Zelenovic so that he's fully aware - and that's the only thing that matters for the Chamber - that he's fully aware as to what he pleads guilty to and to what counts, what incidents, what parts of it he pleads not guilty to. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I hope we will be able to complete this task this afternoon. I would only ask that, if possible, tomorrow's hearing be set at a later time so that I have the opportunity to inform Mr. Zelenovic of whatever is agreed with the Prosecution this afternoon. As for the indictment, I do not need it in B/C/S, but he certainly does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jovanovic, if you would apply with the Registry to have an opportunity to briefly meet with Mr. Zelenovic tomorrow morning, I would say to start with, 15 minutes might do it. It's easy to explain, I take it. And Mr. Zelenovic has been able to follow all of the discussions of today. So therefore, of course, if it would turn out that you haven't got sufficient time to discuss the matter with Mr. Zelenovic, we'll hear an application for further time. But ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that the transportation of Mr. Zelenovic will take place at the usual time. Would 15 minutes, to start with, and so a later start of 15 minutes, which would allow you to see Mr. Zelenovic, would that help you out, to start with?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll adjourn -- yes, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one more clarification. Do you also want us to strike those paragraphs that relate to Gojko Jankovic and Radovan Stankovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's exclusively about them. I think most of them are -- no, they are not stricken out yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So we can do that, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps that would make it -- of course, it doesn't relate in any way to Mr. Zelenovic. But if that's out, it's easier to use it as a working document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, quarter past 9.00, in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 11.26 a.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of January, 2007, at 9.15 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Motion Hearing adjourned at
